title: Assess knowledge, application and engagement
statement: Assess what reading produced in knowledge gained, its application and engagement, not only recall, gist or word-meaning tasks.
detail: The RAND Reading Study Group's 2002 report, in a reading course's digest of it, holds that knowledge, application and engagement are all critical outcomes of reading with comprehension and that assessments reflecting all three are needed (p. xix; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`, line 187). The digest's summary of the report's statement of the problem adds that assessments must capture all three, not just recall, gist or word-meaning tasks (p. 113). It is the study group's recommendation for an assessment system, not a measured result.
against: It is the study group's recommendation for an assessment system, not a measured result.

evidence.quote: Knowledge, application, and engagement are all critical outcomes of reading with comprehension; assessments that reflect all three of these outcomes are needed.

Because knowledge, application, and engagement are held to be the crucial consequences of comprehending text, the RRSG argues assessments must capture all three, not just recall/gist/word-meaning tasks.

citations.ref: RAND Reading Study Group 2002, Reading for Understanding (MR-1465)
